key_insight: Microscopic impurities act as degradation nucleation sites in wide-bandgap perovskite films, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can flag them within seconds.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could help prioritize stable perovskite films for scalable tandem solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation onset.
Detect and quantify impurities with reflected-light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation initiating at impurity–perovskite interfaces, while films with higher impurity density exhibited faster early degradation.
watch_item: The abstract does not report detection accuracy or validate impurity density as a predictor of long-term device lifetime.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
